title: About Us

hero.title: The first and
hero.subtitle: Charles Ogweno flew jets for the Kenya Air Force before he ever touched a turntable. He named the sound Omega One because it was meant to be the only one that lasted. Four decades on, it is the one still standing.

story.title: Our story
story.lede: Omega One has been a household name in western Kenya since 1983 — a mobile disco that grew into a sound company, a concert stage and a recording studio. The rivals it started against, Intercity, Funkatek and Galaxy, are all gone.

milestones.title: Out of the cockpit
milestones.text: Ogweno joins the Kenya Air Force as a flight cadet and trains as a pilot in the UK. After the attempted coup he is detained, and on release he leaves the force for good.

milestones.title: Omega One begins
milestones.text: He names the mobile disco Omega One — the first and the last of its kind. Intercity, Funkatek and Galaxy all came after, and none of them lasted.

milestones.title: The residencies
milestones.text: Years on rotation at Tokyo Omega Lodge in Otonglo and Webbs Club in Kisii, with shows out to Mombasa, Kitale, Kapsabet and Nakuru.

milestones.title: Sound Check Studio
milestones.text: The ground floor of the family house in Kisumu becomes a recording studio. Ohangla maestro Tony Nyadundo and Onyi Papa Jay both cut tracks there.

milestones.title: Still on the road
milestones.text: Full live sound reinforcement for concerts, rallies and the international bands that tour the western region — with the DJs Omega trained now working across Kenya.

items.title: Live sound
items.text: Line array reinforcement — Martin Audio, Turbosound and Electro-Voice — rigged for halls and open grounds.

items.title: Stage and power
items.text: Concert stage build and 130 kVA of generator on site, so the show does not stop with the grid.

items.title: Sound Check Studio
items.text: Tracking and mixing in Kisumu, in the room where Nyadundo and Onyi Papa Jay recorded.

items.title: Mobile disco
items.text: The original business. Benga, ohangla and rumba, read off the floor by DJs who know the room.

items.title: Rallies and tours
items.text: Systems hired to political parties and to international bands playing the western region.

items.title: DJ development
items.text: Don Ben, DJ Mike, Kim and Charley all learned the ropes here before moving on.
